name: MCP servers
summary: Connect Claude Code to outside tools, databases and services through the Model Context Protocol.
what: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard for giving an AI assistant extra tools. An MCP server might expose your issue tracker, a database or a design tool. Once you add a server, Claude can call its tools directly instead of you copying data into the chat. Servers run either on your machine (started as a local command) or remotely over HTTP.

impact.title: Work with your real tools
impact.detail: Claude can read a ticket, query a database or check monitoring data itself, without copy and paste.

impact.title: Share a setup with the team
impact.detail: Servers added at project scope are saved in a .mcp.json file you can commit to the repository.

impact.title: Control what is connected
impact.detail: The /mcp command shows each server's status and lets you reconnect, sign in, enable or disable it.

howItWorks: Add a remote server with claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url>, or a local one with claude mcp add <name> -- <command>.
Pick a scope: local (the default, just you in this project), project (saved to .mcp.json) or user (all your projects).
Servers from a project's .mcp.json wait for your approval before they run.
In a session, use /mcp to check status and to sign in to servers that need OAuth.
Only connect servers you trust: what a server returns can try to steer Claude.
